tasks.short: Analyze site factors and file the diagrams.

steps.what: Read proposed site factors already stored.
Illustrate the findings on those diagrams.

tasks.design: The technician analyzes the proposed site factors, designs the graphs, tracings, and diagrams, and illustrates the findings. {DOCS} only opens factors already stored, then files the diagrams they accepted. Nothing draws a diagram and nothing generates a map. The list of factors is not the analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stored site factors were copied out before the technician could analyze them.
tasks.enabler_now: Site factors the file already holds can be opened again.
tasks.still_hard: What the factors mean, and how to illustrate them, stay with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician designs the diagram. An opened note does not.
tasks.altitude: The analysis, the design, and the illustration stay in full. Only opening stored factors and filing the accepted diagrams are shorter.

reach.learn: The designer does not analyze the site

evidence.claim: A stored activity or complaint can be listed. The technician writes the report or the reply.

assumptions: The workflow starts when proposed site factors are stored and ends when the accepted diagrams are filed. The technician analyzes and draws. Nothing generates a diagram.

The fields are site id, the factor name, and the finding they illustrate. The site file produces the stored factor. The technician produces the finding. A factor that is missing is added by the technician, not invented.
The prior classes this task as amplify. The steps agree the analysis stays. The open and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether the proposed site factors are already written on the file.
Which findings the office will not illustrate until the technician has visited the site.
research_questions: Are the proposed site factors already written on the file?
Which findings will the office not illustrate until the technician has visited the site?

tasks.short: Prepare project reports and file them.

steps.what: Prepare reports of the project activities.

tasks.design: The technician prepares the reports and documents the project activities, then accepts them. {DOCS} only opens activities already recorded, then files the reports they accepted. The open list is not the report. Nothing writes the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities already in the log were copied into the report by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Activities the log already holds can be opened before they write.
tasks.still_hard: What the report should say about those activities stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician writes the report. A log does not.
tasks.altitude: Preparing and accepting the reports stay in full. Only opening recorded activities and filing the accepted reports are shorter.

reach.task: Read the report the technician accepted
reach.learn: The supervisor does not write the report

evidence.claim: A stored activity or complaint can be listed. The technician writes the report or the reply.

assumptions: The workflow starts when project activities are recorded and ends when the accepted report is filed. The technician writes the report. The log does not.

The fields are project id, the activity name, and the date already recorded. The log produces them. The technician produces the report text. An activity that is not in the log is added by the technician.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps disagree in part: writing the report stays. The open and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether every project activity is already on the log.
Which activities the office will not put in a report until the technician has seen them.

tasks.short: Report site problems and negotiate changes.

steps.what: Report maintenance problems occurring at the project site.
Negotiate changes to resolve system conflicts.

tasks.design: The technician reports the maintenance problems occurring at the project site and negotiates the changes that resolve the system conflicts. They accept that version. {EMAIL} sends only the report they accepted. {DOCS} only opens a problem already noted. The call is not recorded. Nothing negotiates the change.
tasks.previous_blocker: A problem already noted was retyped into the report to the supervisor.
tasks.enabler_now: A problem the site note already holds can be opened before they report it.
tasks.still_hard: Which change resolves the conflict stays with the technician in the negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician negotiates. A sent report does not.
tasks.altitude: Reporting and negotiating stay in full. Only opening a noted problem and sending the accepted report are shorter.

reach.task: Receive the report the technician accepted
reach.learn: The supervisor still hears the negotiation from the technician

evidence.claim: A stored activity or complaint can be listed. The technician writes the report or the reply.
Negotiating a price is the technician's decision. A filed price is the one they accepted. It does not close the contract.
This design does not score technicians and does not record calls. A list of open work is not a performance record.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a maintenance problem is noted and ends when the accepted report is sent. The technician reports and negotiates. The send is that accepted version.

The fields are site id, the problem they noted, and the change they accepted. The site note produces the problem when it is already written. The technician produces the change. No accepted change means no report is sent.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the negotiation stays. The open and the send are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether maintenance problems are already written before the technician reports them.
Which system conflicts the office will not negotiate by mail.
research_questions: Are maintenance problems already written before the technician reports them?
Which system conflicts will the office not negotiate by mail?

tasks.short: Inspect the site and file the accepted note.

steps.what: Evaluate contractor work on the site.

tasks.design: The technician inspects the project site, evaluates the contractor's work, detects design malfunctions, and ensures conformance to applicable codes. That acceptance is the note after the visit. {DOCS} files only that version. Nothing inspects the site and nothing decides a malfunction. This file does not certify the building.
tasks.previous_blocker: The note was written up later from memory because the visit itself could not be shortened.
tasks.enabler_now: A note they have already accepted after the visit can be filed without retyping it.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the work conforms, on the site, stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician inspects. A filed note does not.
tasks.altitude: The inspection, the evaluation, and the conformance check stay in full. Only filing the note they accepted after the visit is shorter.

reach.task: Read the inspection the technician accepted
reach.learn: The supervisor does not inspect the site

evidence.claim: A site inspection is the technician's observation. The file is the note they accepted after the visit. It is not a generated finding.

A tool that assigns work from a worker's performance, or that decides a safety outcome, is not used here. The technician evaluates conformance. National building rules differ on who may certify the work. This file does not certify it.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the technician is on the project site and ends when the note they accepted after the visit is filed. The inspection happens before that acceptance. Nothing certifies the building.
The fields are site id, the malfunction they detected, and conform or not. The technician produces them on the visit. A malfunction they did not see is not filed.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the inspection stays. Filing the accepted note is the part that moves.
unknowns: Whether applicable codes for this site are already named on the job file.
Which malfunctions the office will not treat as closed until a second visit.
